AccessibilityPayload.description: Phase 5. No score, by design: violation counts are not a conformance measure.

coverage_note.default: Automated rules detect a subset of WCAG issues. A clean result does not mean a site is accessible; conformance requires manual testing and expert review.
coverage_note.title: Coverage Note

AccessibilityPayload.title: AccessibilityPayload

AnalyzerRun.description: Outcome of one analyzer within one scan. Present even when it did not run.
AnalyzerRun.title: AnalyzerRun

AppliedCap.description: A band ceiling triggered by a dominant observation.
AppliedCap.title: AppliedCap

ArchitecturePayload.description: Phase 3. Rendering strategy signals, platform indicators, runtime observations.
ArchitecturePayload.title: ArchitecturePayload

AxeObservation.description:
Results from the vendored, pinned axe-core build.

``engine_version`` is recorded because rule sets change between versions, so a stored
result is only interpretable against the engine that produced it.
AxeObservation.title: AxeObservation

Confidence.description:
Internal reasoning metadata.

Used only to derive :class:`FindingStatus`. Never rendered next to a claim: a
percentage or grade beside an uncertain statement reads as authority and launders a
guess into a fact.
Confidence.title: Confidence

DesignPayload.description:
Phase 4. Palette, typography, spacing/radius/shadow scales, layout, media, motion.

``coverage`` is declared now because every design claim must be reported alongside the
sample it came from.
DesignPayload.title: DesignPayload

DetectedProduct.description: A technology detected from observable signals.

signal_summary.description: Human-readable list of the signals that matched.
signal_summary.title: Signal Summary

version.description: Only set when a signature captured a version explicitly.
version.title: Version

DetectedProduct.title: DetectedProduct

ErrorCode.description: Machine-readable error identity, shared by problem responses and scan errors.
ErrorCode.title: ErrorCode

EvidenceKind.description: What kind of observation an :class:`~weblens.domain.evidence.EvidenceRef` points at.
EvidenceKind.title: EvidenceKind

EvidenceRef.description:
A pointer to the observation that supports a finding, with a quotable excerpt.

Deliberately self-contained rather than an index into a separate evidence store:
findings travel alone into report files and IndexedDB, so each carries the bounded,
sanitized excerpt it needs. ``RawEvidence`` itself is never returned by the API.

excerpt.description: Sanitized, truncated raw value as observed.
excerpt.title: Excerpt

location.description: Absolute URL, CSS selector, or header name.
location.title: Location

source.description: Machine path into the evidence, e.g. 'http.headers.content-security-policy'.
source.title: Source

EvidenceRef.title: EvidenceRef

dropped_claims.description: Statements removed because they could not be traced to a finding.
dropped_claims.title: Dropped Claims

Finding.description: One structured conclusion about one property of the target.

confidence.description: Internal reasoning metadata used to derive status. Not a user-facing qualifier - see docs/blueprint/decisions.md D5.

detected.description: None when the notion of detection does not apply.
detected.title: Detected

reason.description: Required for every negative status: why not.
reason.title: Reason

source.description: Id of the analyzer that produced this finding.
source.title: Source

Finding.title: Finding

FindingStatus.description:
User-facing certainty of a finding.

The three negative states are deliberately distinct: they answer different questions
and conflating them is how a tool starts making things up.
FindingStatus.title: FindingStatus

HeaderEntry.description:
One response header. Duplicates are preserved as separate entries.

Collapsing duplicate headers loses information that matters (multiple ``Set-Cookie``
lines, repeated ``Content-Security-Policy``), so the list keeps them intact.
HeaderEntry.title: HeaderEntry

Interpretation.description:
A subjective statement derived from findings, kept structurally separate from them.

Interpretations cannot be built without citing findings, and only analyzers whose job
is interpretation emit them. That is how "observed fact" and "our reading of it" stay
apart in the API, the UI, and every generated report.

basis.description: Finding ids this reading is derived from.
basis.title: Basis

caveat.default: Interpretation derived from observed values, not a directly observed fact.
caveat.title: Caveat

Interpretation.title: Interpretation

MetadataObservation.description: Document metadata as served. Lengths are reported because they are actionable.
MetadataObservation.title: MetadataObservation

grounded_in.description: Finding ids the text cites. Every sentence must cite at least one.
grounded_in.title: Grounded In

NetworkRequestRecord.description:
One request/response pair observed during navigation.

``Set-Cookie`` values and authorization headers are never captured; only the selected
cache/CORS/security headers listed by the collector reach this record.
NetworkRequestRecord.title: NetworkRequestRecord

PerformanceObservation.description: Single cold lab run at a bounded settle point. Not field data (see L-PERF-01).
PerformanceObservation.title: PerformanceObservation

PerformancePayload.description: Phase 5. Run context lives on scan metadata and applies to every metric here.
PerformancePayload.title: PerformancePayload

type.description: Stable URI identifying the problem kind.
type.title: Type

RuleOutcome.description: Outcome of one security scoring rule.
RuleOutcome.title: RuleOutcome

RunContext.description:
The conditions the measurements were taken under.

Performance and design numbers are meaningless without this, so it travels with every
result and is printed in every report.

collection_mode.description: 'http_only' or 'browser'. Tells the reader which evidence base was used.
collection_mode.title: Collection Mode

user_agent.default: WebLens/0.1.0 (+https://github.com/weblens; passive website analyzer; respects robots.txt)
user_agent.title: User Agent

RunContext.title: RunContext

SampleCoverage.description:
How much of the page the style sample actually covers.

Reported alongside every design finding: a claim about "the" border radius of a page
means little without knowing it came from 1500 of 40000 elements.
SampleCoverage.title: SampleCoverage

ScanError.description: A failure recorded on a result rather than raised to the caller.

subject.description: Stage key or analyzer id the failure belongs to.
subject.title: Subject

ScanError.title: ScanError

ScanOptions.description: Per-scan options. ``extra='forbid'`` so an option typo is a 422, not a silent no-op.

sections.description: Restrict analysis to these sections. None means all.
sections.title: Sections

ScanOptions.title: ScanOptions

url.description: Public http(s) URL. Normalized and guarded server-side.
url.title: Url

ScreenshotRef.description:
Screenshot metadata plus inline data.

The client moves the bytes into its own IndexedDB store as a Blob and does not keep them
in the result record, which is why this is a separate top-level list rather than being
buried inside the design payload.
ScreenshotRef.title: ScreenshotRef

SectionKey.description: The eight report sections. Order here is the canonical presentation order.
SectionKey.title: SectionKey

SectionSet.description: All eight sections, as explicit fields so both sides of the wire stay typed.
SectionSet.title: SectionSet

SecurityPayload.description: Phase 2. ``score`` is the only score in the whole domain model (axiom A4).
SecurityPayload.title: SecurityPayload

rationale.description: Why this outcome, stated in observable terms.
rationale.title: Rationale

weight.description: Points available when the rule is applicable.
weight.title: Weight

disclaimer.default: This is a passive assessment of externally observable configuration for a single page at a single point in time. It does not evaluate application logic, server-side controls, dependencies, or data handling, and it cannot establish that a site is secure or insecure.
disclaimer.title: Disclaimer

points_applicable.description: Sum of weights for evaluated rules only; excluded rules are not counted.
points_applicable.title: Points Applicable

StageKey.description: Collection and analysis stages, in execution order.
StageKey.title: StageKey

StageProgress.description:
Progress derived from stages that actually completed.

There is no interpolation and no time-based estimate here on purpose: the requirement
is honest progress, and the simplest way to guarantee it is to have no mechanism
capable of faking it.
StageProgress.title: StageProgress

TargetInfo.description: What we ended up analyzing, which is not always what was requested.
TargetInfo.title: TargetInfo

info.description:
Evidence-based website technical intelligence.

Detection is deterministic and never performed by an AI model. Every asserted fact carries the
evidence that supports it, and anything that cannot be established from observation is reported
as not detected, not determinable, or unable to verify rather than guessed.

Analysis is passive: WebLens observes what a normal visit reveals. It does not test
authentication, submit forms, fuzz inputs, or attempt to bypass access controls.
info.title: WebLens API

post.summary: Generate an explanation over verified findings

get.summary: Analyzers, stages, and limits in this build

delete.description:
Called by the client once the result is stored in IndexedDB.

Idempotent: an unknown id also returns 204, because the desired end state - no server copy -
holds either way.
delete.summary: Release the server-side copy of a scan

409.description: The scan has not finished yet.

410.description: The result was released after the retention window.

get.description:
Report service liveness and whether a browser is available.

``status`` stays ``ok`` when the browser is missing: the API is up and HTTP-only scans still
work. The frontend uses ``browser.available`` to warn before a scan instead of after.
